from *anna* ending in the accusative case, the suffix *ṇa* occurs in the sense of one who has obtained it; thus, *ānnaḥ*.
(3.4.85) *vaśaṃ gataḥ*: when the sense is "having come under control," [the suffix] *yat* occurs. Example: *vaśyaḥ*. (3.4.86) *padam asmin dṛśyam*: when the word *pada* is seen in this [sūtra].

The suffix *yat* occurs after a word ending in the nominative case in the sense of "that which is seen in this" (*dṛśyam asmin*). Example: *padyaḥ kardamaḥ* ("mud that is found in water"). [Rule 3.4.87:

After the word *mūla* ending in the nominative case, the suffix *yat* occurs in the sense of "belonging to this" (*asya*), provided that the root is not firm (*na tac cen mūlaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhavati*). Examples: *mūlyā māṣāḥ*, *mūlyā mudgāḥ*. [This means] they have loose roots; the sense is that they have not grown well.

*Dhenuṣyā* and *gārhapatya* are irregularly formed (*nipātyete*) as technical names (*saṃjñā*). In the case of *dhenuṣyā*, the suffix *yat* is applied to a cow given for the purpose of providing milk, and the augment *ṣuk* is added. In the case of *gārhapatya*, the suffix *ñya* is applied to a specific fire associated with the master of the house (*gṛhapati*).
[Pāṇini 3.4.89: *Mūlena anāmye*.

The suffix *yat* occurs after a word ending in the third case (*tṛtīyā*), beginning with *mūla*, when the sense is "not to be bent" (*anāmya*). Thus, that which is not to be bent by the root is *mūlyam*. The suffix *ṇyat* is used here precisely because of this rule, despite the general prohibition against using *ṇyat* after a word ending in *mūla*. [This applies] only when the sense is "not to be bent": wood that is not to be bent by the root is simply *mūlenānāmyaṃ kāṣṭham*.

And by the rule *vayasā ca tulye* (Pāṇini 5.1.117), the suffix *yat* occurs after a word ending in the third case, beginning with *vayas* or *mūla*, when the sense is "equal to" (*tulya*). That which is equal in age is *vayasyaḥ*. That which is equal in price is *mūlyaḥ paṭaḥ* ("a cloth of equivalent value"). [This applies] only when the sense is "equal to": an enemy who is equal in age is simply *vayasā tulyo ripuḥ*.

(3.4.91) *nau-tūla-aviṣaiḥ tārya-saṃmita-vadhyeṣu*: [The suffix] occurs after words such as *nau* ending in the third case, when the meanings of "crossable" (*tārya*) and so forth are expressed. *By boat, crossable* (*nāvā tāryam*): *nāvyam* water. *Measured by a scale* (*tulayā saṃmitam*): *tulyam*. Even though not measured, [the suffix applies] because of the governing rule (88) "also in names" (*asaṃmitam api nāmni*). Or, because it is determined by comparison with a scale. *To be killed by poison* (*viṣeṇa vadhyaḥ*): *viṣyaḥ*. (3.4.92) *sītayā saṃmite*.
The suffix *yat* occurs after the word *sītā* ending in the third case when the meaning is "cultivated" (*samita*). For example: *sītayā samitam* = *sītyam*; *dvisītyam*; *trisītyam*.

Regarding the rule *dharmeṇa prāpye* (Pāṇini 5.1.102): the suffix *yat* occurs after the word *dharma* ending in the third case when the meaning is "attainable through" (*prāpya*). For example: *dharmyaḥ*.

(3.4.94) *Anapeta* [is used] after words beginning with *pathin*, as well as after *dharma*, provided they are in the ablative case, when something is not deviating from them. That which does not deviate from the *path* is *pathya*; likewise, *arthyam*, *nyāyyam*, and *dharmyam*. Because of the governing rule *nāmni* (88), this refers to that which does not deviate from the path of action; thus, *bheṣaja* (medicine) alone is *pathya*, and not the village path.
(3.4.95) *Nirmita* [is used] after *chandas*.
The suffix *yat* occurs after the word *chandas* ending in the third case when the sense of "produced from" (*nirmita*) is expressed. Thus: *chandasya*.
By rule 3.4.96, *uras-aṇ-cha*:
the suffix *aṇ* and *yat* occur after the word *uras* ending in the third case when the sense of "produced from" is expressed. Thus: *aurasaḥ putraḥ* ("a son born from the breast") and *urasyaḥ*.

(3.4.97) *hṛdayasya priye*: after the word *hṛdaya* ending in the genitive case, the suffix *yat* occurs in the sense of "beloved. Thus, *hṛdyaḥ*. Since the state of being beloved exists indeed in the context of a mantra for subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), as well as in Vedic and other contexts where one makes someone dear, this [suffix] is established by this very rule. (3.4.98) *matajanayoḥ karaṇajalpayoḥ*: [The suffix *yat* occurs] after *mata* and *jana* in the senses of "instrument" and "talk," respectively.

That which occurs after the words *mata* and *jana*, when they have the senses of "instrument" (*karaṇa*) and "speech" (*jalpa*) respectively: from *mata* [in the sense of] instrument, state, or means, we get *matyam*. From *jana* [in the sense of] speech, we get *janya*.
Regarding *hala* in the rule 3.4.99 (*halasya karṣe*):

that which occurs after *hala* ending in the genitive case, in the sense of "ploughing" (*karṣa*), whether as a state or a means, is *halyaḥ*. *Dvihalyaḥ*. Because it is a qualifier, the rule applies to that which ends in [the word *hala*].

*tatra sādhuḥ* (Pāṇini 3.4.100): after a word ending in the locative case, the suffix *yat* occurs in the sense of "good for that. For example: *karmaṇi sādhuḥ* ("good for action") results in *karmaṇyaḥ*; *śaraṇyaḥ* ("good for refuge"); *sabhyaḥ* ("good for the assembly"). *Sādhuḥ* means skillful, fit, or beneficial. *pratijanādibhyaḥ khañ* (Pāṇini 3.4.101).

The suffix *khañ* occurs after *pratijana* and other words in the sense of "one who is skilled (*sādhu*) therein. For example: one who is skilled among people (*pratijane sādhuḥ*) is *prātijanīnaḥ*. Similarly, *aidaṃyugīnaḥ*. The [words] *pratijana*, *idaṃyuga*, *saṃyuga*, *samayuga*, *parayuga*, *parakula*, *amuṣyakula*, *sarvajana*, *viśvajana*, *pañcajana*, and *mahājana* [are included].
By rule 3.4.102, *bhaktāt* [is used]: the suffix *ṇa* occurs after *bhakta* in the sense of "one who is skilled therein. For example: *bhāktaḥ*.
*pariṣado ṇyaś ca* (3.4.103): In the sense of "one who is fit for that," the suffix *ṇya* is applied after the word *pariṣad*, and the suffix *ṇa* is also applied. Thus: *pāriṣadyaḥ* and *pāriṣadaḥ*.
*kathādibhyaṣ ṭhak* (3.4.104).

The suffix *ṭhak* occurs after the words beginning with *kathā* in the sense of "one who is proficient in that. Examples: *kāthikaḥ*, *vaikathikaḥ*. [The list is: *kathā*, *vikathā*, *viśvakathā*, *vitaṇḍā*, *janavāda*, *vṛtti*, *saṃgraha*, *guṇa*, *gaṇa*, *āyurveda*, *guḍa*, *kulmāṣa*, *ikṣu*, *saktu*, *apūpa*, *māṃsaudana*, *veṇu*, *saṃgrāma*, *saṃghāta*, *pravāsa*, *nivāsa*, *upavāsa*.
[Furthermore,] the suffix *ḍhañ* occurs after *pathin*, *atithi*, *vasati*, and *svapati* (Pāṇini 4.4.105).

In this context, namely regarding that which is "suitable" (*sādhu*) for things such as provisions for a journey (*pathya*), the suffix *ḍhañ* occurs. Examples: *pātheyaḥ*, *ātitheyaḥ*, *vāsateyaḥ*, *svāpateyaḥ*.

Regarding the rule *samānodare śayitaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.4.106): the suffix *yat* occurs after the word *samānodara* ending in the seventh case, in the sense of "one who has slept [there]. Examples: *samānodaryaḥ*, *sodaryaḥ*.
The third chapter is completed.
Regarding the rule *prāk krītāc chaḥ* (4.1.1): it should be understood that the suffix *cha* applies up to the limit of the word *krīta*.

*ugavādibhyo yat* (Pāṇini 4.1.2): The suffix *yat* occurs after words ending in *u* and after the group beginning with *go* when the sense is that of a derivative product (*chavi*). Examples: *śaṅkavyaṃ dāru* ("wood for a stake"), *picavyaḥ karpāsaḥ* ("cotton for a brush"). *sanaṅgavyaṃ carma*, *caravyās taṇḍulāḥ*, *saktavyā dhānāḥ*. *gavyaṃ vanam*, *haviṣyās taṇḍulāḥ*. [The following are included in the *go-ādi* group: *go*, *havis*, *aṣṭakā*, *barhis*, *yuga*, *medhā*, *sruc*, and for *nābhi*, the substitution of *nabha*; e.g., *nabhyaṃ kāṣṭham* ("wood for a nave"). After *śvan*, the suffix *yaṇ* is applied, and the vowel may optionally be long: *śunyam*, *śūnyam*. After *ūdhas*, the suffix *na* is applied.

*Ūdhanyaḥ kūpaḥ* ("a well for a cow's udder"). Since the rule *gor aci yat* (Pāṇini 5.1.2) already establishes this, the repetition here is for the purpose of making known the application of the suffix to a compound ending in *go*: *sugavyam*, *pratigavyam*. *Kambalyam ūrṇāpalaśatam* ("a hundred palas of wool [forming] a *kambalya*") is established by the rule *vistācitakambalyāt* (Pāṇini 5.1.31).
*Vā haviryūpādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.3).

The suffix *yat* is applied after words denoting sacrificial offerings (*havirvacana*) and after words such as *yūpa*, when the sense is "suitable for" (*chaviṣaya*). For example: *taṇḍulāḥ puroḍāśyāḥ* ("rice grains suitable for a *puroḍāśa* cake") and *puroḍāśīyāḥ*. After the word *havis*, the suffix is applied invariably by the preceding rule [Pāṇini 4.3.70]. Examples: *yūpyaṃ kāṣṭham* ("wood suitable for a sacrificial post") and *yūpīyam*; *dīpyam* and *dīpīyam*. [The suffix is also applied] after *yūpa*, *dīpa*, *apūpa*, *taṇḍula*, *pṛthuka*, *abhyūṣa*, *abhyoṣa*, *avoṣa*, *kiṇva*, *musala*, *kaṭaka*, *karṇaveṣṭaka*, *irgala*, *sthūṇā*, *aśvapattra*, and after words denoting modifications of food (*annavikāra*): e.g., *suryam* and *surīyam*. By the rule of extension to that which ends in such a word (*tadantavidhi*), we have: *pradīpyam* and *pradīpīyam*; *yavāpūpyam* and *yavāpūpīyam*.
(4.1.4) *tasmai hitam* ("beneficial for that"):

after a word ending in the fourth case, the suffixes *cha* and *yat* are applied according to the rules in the sense of "beneficial. For example: *vatsīyaḥ* ("beneficial for calves") and *avatsīyaḥ* ("not beneficial for calves") from *godhuk* ("cowherd"), meaning one who is beneficial to calves; *paṭavyaḥ* ("beneficial for cloth").
(4.1.5) Not so, however, after the words *rājan*, *ācārya*, *vṛṣan*, or *brāhmaṇa*.

The suffix *cha* does not occur after these [words] when the sense is "beneficial for" (*hita*). For example: *rājñe hitam* ("beneficial for the king"), *ācāryāya hitam* ("beneficial for the teacher"), *vṛṣṇe hitam* ("beneficial for the bull"), *brāhmaṇāya hitam* ("beneficial for the brahmin").
Regarding the rule *dehāṃśād yat* (Pāṇini 4.1.6):

the suffix *yat* occurs after a word denoting a part of the body (*śarīrāvayava*) when the sense is "beneficial for. For example: *dantebhyo hitam*, *dantyam* ("beneficial for the teeth"); *rājadantyam* ("beneficial for the front teeth"); *nābhyam* ("beneficial for the navel"). Here, there is no substitution of *nabha-* [for *nābhi-*], because it is a part of a living being (*prāṇyaṅga*).

From *khala*, *yava*, *māṣa*, *tila*, *vṛṣa*, *brahman*, and *ratha* [the suffix *yat* is applied] in the sense of being beneficial (*hita*). That which is beneficial for a threshing floor is *khalya*; likewise, *yavya*, *māṣya*, and *tilya*. That which is beneficial for a bull is *vṛṣya*. That which is beneficial for Brahmins is *brahmaṇya*. That which is beneficial for a chariot is *rathyā* (a carriage-road).
From *aja* and *avi*, the suffix *thyan* [is applied]. (Pāṇini 4.1.8)
The suffix *thyan* occurs in the sense of "beneficial for" (*hite*) after these two [words]. Examples: *ajathyā*, *avithyā*.
The suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "beneficial for" after words ending in *bhoga* and after the word *ātman*. Examples: *mātṛbhogīnaḥ*, *rājabhogīnaḥ*, *ācāryabhogīnaḥ*; *ātmanīnaḥ*.

(4.1.10) *pañcaviśvāj janāntāt tadarthāt*: After the words *pañca* and *viśva*, when they end in *jana* and denote "people," the suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "beneficial for that. [Examples: beneficial for five people (*pañcabhyo janebhyo hitaḥ*) = *pañcajanīnaḥ*; beneficial for all people (*viśvajanīnaḥ*). Why does it say "in the sense of that" (*tadarthāt*)? Consider: one whose people are all is *viśvajanaḥ*; beneficial for him (*tasmai hitaḥ*), or beneficial for all people (*viśveṣāṃ janāya vā hitaḥ*), is *viśvajanīyaḥ*. (4.1.11) *sarvāt*.

The suffix *kha* occurs after the word *sarva* ending in *jana*, in the sense of "beneficial for" (*dhita*). Example: *sarvajanīnaḥ*. It is only when [the compound] has that meaning [i.e., "beneficial for"] that [this applies]; otherwise: *sarvajanīyaḥ*. And by rule 4.1.12, *mahataś ca ṭhañ*:

the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after the word *mahat* and after the word *sarva* ending in *jana*, in the sense of "beneficial for. Examples: *māhājanikaḥ*, *sārvajanikaḥ*. It is only when [the compound] has that meaning [i.e., "beneficial for"] that [this applies]; otherwise: *mahājanīyaḥ*, *sarvajanīyaḥ*.
(4.1.13) *sarvāṇ ṇo vā*:

after the word *sarva*, the suffix *ṇa* optionally occurs in the sense of "beneficial for" (*hita*). Thus, that which is beneficial for all is *sārva* or *sarvīya*. The repetition of the mention of *sarva* is for the purpose of excluding [the application of this rule to] words ending in *jana*.
(4.1.14) *puruṣāḍ ḍhañ*: after the word *puruṣa*, the suffix *ḍhañ* occurs.
The suffix *ḍhañ* occurs in the sense of "beneficial for" (*hita*) when following the word *puruṣa*. [Thus: beneficial for a person (*puruṣa*), *pauruṣeya*.

By the rule *māṇavacarakāt khañ* (Pāṇini 4.1.15), the suffix *khañ* occurs in the sense of "beneficial for" after these two words. [Thus: beneficial for a young student, *māṇavīna*; beneficial for a spy, *cārakīṇa*.

(4.1.16) *vikṛteḥ prakṛtau*: When the *prakṛti* (material cause) is to be expressed, the suffixes *cha* and *yat* are applied according to the rules after a word denoting the *vikṛti* (the product) ending in the fourth case. Examples: *aṅgārebhyaḥ kāṣṭhāni*, *aṅgārīyāṇi* ("wood for charcoal"); *picavyaḥ karpāsaḥ* ("cotton from the *picu* plant"). Why "of the *vikṛti*"? [Consider: *udakāya kūpaḥ* ("a well for water"). By the mention of *prakṛti*, the mere cause is understood, so these two suffixes would apply here too. However, because of association with the *vikṛti*, only the material cause (*upādānakāraṇa*) is taken. Why "in the *prakṛti*"? [Consider: *asaye kośī* ("a sheath for a sword").

In the absence of the mention of the *prakṛti* (base), those two suffixes would apply even to other modifications (*vikṛti*) merely for its sake. Thus, *tasmai* [is used] as in: *saktūnāṃ dhānāḥ* ("barley-grits for the sake of barley-meal"). Why does it not occur here: *mūtrāya kalpate yavāgūḥ* ("the gruel serves for urine")? Because of its being dependent (*sāpekṣatva*). Regarding *ṛṣabhopānaho ñyaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.3.17):

the suffix *ñya* occurs after *ṛṣabha* and *upānah* when the base itself is to be expressed. Examples: *ṛṣabhāya vatsaḥ* ("a calf for the bull") → *ārṣabhyaḥ*; *upānahbhyāṃ muñjaḥ* ("muñja grass for sandals") → *aupānahyaḥ*; *upānahbhyāṃ carma* ("leather for sandals") → *aupānahyam*.
*Carmaṇy añ* (4.1.18):

When "hide" (*carman*) is the intended sense as the raw material (*prakṛti*), the suffix *añ* occurs after a word denoting its modification (*vikṛti*). Example: *vāratraṃ carma* ("a hide made of goat-skin").
*Chadirbhalibhyāṃ ḍhañ* (4.1.19).

The suffix *ḍhañ* occurs after these two [stems], when the base meaning (*prakṛti*) is to be expressed. For example: *chādiṣeyāṇi tṛṇāni* ("grass for covering"), *chādiṣeyaṃ carma* ("leather for covering"), and *bāleyās taṇḍulāḥ* ("rice for feeding pigs"). By means of a formal split in the rule (*yogavibhāga*), the suffix *ḍhañ* occurs after the word *upadhi* in its own sense (*svārthe*): that which is simply *upadhi* is called *aupadheya*.

Regarding the rule *tad asyātra syād iti* (Pāṇini 4.1.21): the suffixes *cha* and *yat* occur after a word ending in the nominative case to express the sense of the genitive or the locative, provided that which ends in the nominative is what "might exist" (*syāt*). The verb *syāt* is used in the potential mood (*liṅ*) to denote possibility; the particle *iti* indicates the intended meaning [of the speaker]. Examples: *prāsādo 'sya syāt* ("a palace might belong to him") → *prāsādīyaṃ dāru* ("wood suitable for a palace"). *paraśavyam ayaḥ* ("iron suitable for an axe"). *prāsādo 'tra syāt* ("a palace might be here") → *prāsādīyo deśaḥ* ("a region suitable for a palace"). Why is *syāt* used? [To distinguish from actual existence: *prāsādo 'trāsti* ("a palace exists here"). Why is *iti* used? [To exclude unintended meanings: *prāsādo 'sya Devadattasya syāt* ("a palace might belong to this Devadatta" [but it does not]). The rule *parikhāyā ḍhañ* (Pāṇini 4.1.22) follows.

The suffix *ḍhañ* occurs after the word *parikhā*, which ends in the first case (*prathamā*), in the sense of "belonging to this" (*asyātra syāt*). For example: *pārikheyaḥ deśaḥ* ("a region belonging to a moat").
Regarding the rule *prāg vateṣ ṭhañ* (Pāṇini 4.1.23), the suffix *ṭhañ* should be understood as applying prior to the mention of the term *vati*.

*Saṃkhyādeś cālukaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.24). From here onwards, prior to *vati*, it should be understood that the rule applies to words beginning with a numeral, whether they end in an elided suffix (*aluk*) or not. Example: *dvaipārāyaṇikaḥ*. Why "elided suffix" (*aluka*)? [Counter-examples: *dviśūrpam* (purchased for two *śūrpa*s); *dviśaurpikam* (purchased with two *śūrpa*s). *Ārhāt* (Pāṇini 4.1.25).
Regarding those meanings up to the word *ārhá*, the subsequent rule should be understood as applicable.
[Pāṇini 4.1.26] *kaṃsārdhāṭ ṭhaṭ*: after the words *kaṃsa* and *ardha*, the suffix *ṭhaṅ* occurs, up to [the limit of] *ārhát*. Examples: *kāṃsikaḥ*, *kāṃsikī*; *ārdhikaḥ*, *ārdhikī*.
(4.1.27) *kārṣāpaṇāt*:
after the word *kārṣāpaṇa*, the suffix *ṭhaṅ* occurs in the sense of things worthy of it (*ārhīya*). [Examples: *kārṣāpaṇikaḥ*, *kārṣāpaṇikī*.
(4.1.28) *pratir vāsya*: or, the word *prati* may optionally take its place.

In place of the word *kārṣāpaṇa*, *pratya* is optionally substituted when the suffix *ṭhaṭ* follows. Thus: *pratikaḥ*, *pratikī*. From the word *śūrpa*, the suffix *añ* is optionally applied [by 4.1.29]. Thus: *śaurpaḥ*; [with *ṭhaṭ*: ] *śaurpikaḥ*, *śaurpikī*.
The suffix *aṇ* occurs after these: *sahasra*, *vasana*, *viṃśatika*, and *śatamāna*. [Examples: *sāhasraḥ*, *vāsanaḥ*, *vaiṃśatikaḥ*, *śātamānaḥ*.
After the word *śata* alone, the suffixes *ṭhan* and *ṭyan* occur when it does not mean "interest. (Pāṇini 4.1.31)

The suffixes *ṭhan* and *ṭya* occur after the word *śata* alone, provided that this same "hundred" is not the object denoted [by the derivative]. Thus: *śatikaḥ*, *śatyaḥ*. Why say "after the word alone"? Consider *dviśatam* (two hundred); what is bought for that is *dviśatakam*. Why say "provided it is not that [very hundred]"? Consider *śatakaṃ nidānam* (a set of one hundred threads). However, when it refers to another hundred, the suffixes certainly do occur: *śatena krītaṃ śāṭakaśatam* (a hundred garments bought for a hundred) is *śatikam* or *śatyam*.
[Furthermore: *kan* occurs after a numeral other than *atiśata* (Pāṇini 4.1.32).

The suffix *kan* is added after a numeral, excluding those ending in *tya* and *śat*. Examples: *pañcakaḥ*, *bahukaḥ*. Why say "excluding [those ending in] *atiśata*"? [Because otherwise it would apply to] *āśītikaḥ* and *cātvāriṃśatkaḥ*.

The words *kati* and *gaṇa* are treated in the same way (Pāṇini 4.1.33): the word *kati* and the word *gaṇa* are to be regarded everywhere as numerals. Examples: *katikaḥ*, *gaṇakaḥ*. Elsewhere also: *katidhā*, *gaṇadhā*; *katiśaḥ*, *gaṇaśaḥ*; *katikṛtvaḥ*, *gaṇakṛtvaḥ*.
(4.1.34) For that which ends in *vat*, the grammatical operation pertaining to a numeral also occurs elsewhere. Thus: *tāvatkaḥ*, *tāvatkṛtvaḥ*.
(4.1.35) The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied.
The suffix *kan* optionally takes the augment *iṭ* when it is connected with a word ending in *vat*. Thus: *tāvatikaḥ* or *tāvatkaḥ*.
According to Pāṇini 4.1.36, the suffix *kan* occurs after the words *viṃśati* and *triṃśat*. Thus: *viṃśatikaḥ*, *triṃśatkaḥ*.
*anāmni ḍvun* (Pāṇini 4.1.37):

When it is not a name (*asaṃjñā*), the suffix *ḍvun* is applied after the words *viṃśati* and *triṃśat*. Thus, *viṃśakaḥ* ("worth twenty") and *triṃśakaḥ* ("worth thirty"). Why "when it is not a name"? [Because in names] we have *viṃśatikaḥ* and *triṃśatkaḥ*.

*saṃkhyādhyardhādeḥ saṃkhyeyāl lug adviḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.38): After a word beginning with *adhyardha* or a numeral, when denoting the thing numbered (*saṃkhyeya*), there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix, provided it is not *dvi*.

The elision (*luk*) of the suffix prescribed after a numeral beginning with *adhyardha* and ending in a countable noun (*saṃkhyeya*) occurs only once, and not twice. Examples: *dviśūrpaḥ*, *pañcaśūrpaḥ*, *adhyardhaśūrpaḥ*, *ardhapañcamaḥ*, *adhyardhapañcamaḥ*. Why specify "after a numeral beginning with *adhyardha*" (*saṃkhyādhyardhādeḥ*)? Consider: *paramanaiṣkikam*. Why specify "ending in a countable noun" (*saṃkhyeyāt*)? Consider: *ekādaśakaḥ*. Why specify "not twice" (*advir*)? Consider: *dviśaurpikam* (meaning "bought for two *śūrpa*s"). The restriction "not when it is a conventional name" (*anāmnī*) applies as well: *pāñcalohitikaḥ*, *pāñcakārṣāpaṇikaḥ*.
The inclusion of the term *adhyardha* is for the purpose of precluding the application of other numeral-related grammatical operations elsewhere.

(4.1.39) After the words *kārṣāpaṇasahasra*, *suvarṇaśata*, and *māna*, as well as after these same words when preceded by the numerals *dvi* and *adhyardha*, the suffix prescribed [by 5.1.28] may optionally be elided. Examples: *dvikārṣāpaṇaḥ* or *dvikārṣāpaṇikaḥ*. *adhyardhakārṣāpaṇaḥ* or *adhyardhakārṣāpaṇikaḥ*. *dvisahasram* or *dvisāhasram*. *adhyardhasahasram* or *adhyardhasāhasram*. *dvisuvarṇam* or *dvisauvarṇikam*. *adhyardhasuvarṇam* or *adhyardhasauvarṇikam*. *dviśatamānam* or *dviśātamānam*.

*adhyardhaśatamānam*, *adhyardhaśātamānam*. According to Pāṇini 4.1.40, *dvitribahvāder niṣkavistāt*, there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of the suffix prescribed after *niṣka* and *vistā* when preceded by *dvi*, *tri*, or a word meaning "many" (*bahu*). Thus: *dviniṣkam*, *dvinaiṣkikam*; *triniṣkam*, *trinaiṣkikam*; *bahuniṣkam*, *bahunaiṣkikam*. *dvivistam*, *dvivaistikam*; *trivistam*, *trivaistikam*; *bahuvistam*, *bahuvaistikam*.

From *viṃśatika*, the suffix *kha* is applied (Pāṇini 4.1.41). After a word meaning a number or preceded by *adhyardha*, the suffix *kha* occurs after *viṃśatika*. For example: *dviviṃśatikīnaḥ* ("worth two *viṃśatikas*") and *adhyardhaviṃśatikīnaḥ* ("worth one and a half *viṃśatikas*"). From *khārī*, *kākaṇī*, and so forth, the suffix *īkan* is applied (Pāṇini 4.1.42).

The suffix *īkan* occurs after the words *khārī* and *kākaṇī*, both when preceded by the numeral *adhyardha* and by numerals [in the plural], as well as when used alone. Examples: *dvikhārīkaḥ*, *adhyardhakhārīkaḥ*, *khārīkaḥ*; *dvikākaṇīkam*, *adhyardhakākaṇīkam*, *kākaṇīkam*.

By the rule *paṇapādamāṣād yat* (Pāṇini 5.1.34), the suffix *yat* occurs after these words—*paṇa*, *pāda*, and *māṣa*—when preceded by a numeral or *adhyardha*. Examples: *dvipaṇyaḥ*, *adhyardhapaṇyaḥ*; *dvipādyam*, *adhyardhapādyam*. Because it is not a limb of a living being (*aprāṇyaṅga*), the substitution of *pad* [for *pāda*] does not take place. Examples: *dvimāṣyam*, *adhyardhamāṣyam*.
(4.1.44) After the word *śata* preceded by a numeral or by *adhyardha*, the suffix *ya* optionally occurs. For example: *dviśatyam* or *dviśatam*; *adhyardhaśatyam* or *adhyardhaśatam*.
(4.1.45) [The suffix *ya* also occurs] after the word *śāṇa*.
After a word beginning with *adhyardha* or a numeral, when followed by *śāṇa*, the suffix *ya* is optionally applied. Thus: *dviśāṇyam*, *dviśāṇam*; *adhyardhaśāṇyam*, *adhyardhaśāṇam*.
Regarding the rule *dvitryāder aṇ ca* (Pāṇini 4.1.46):

after the word *śāṇa* preceded by the numerals *dvi* or *tri*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied, and *ya* is also optionally applied. Thus: *dvaiśāṇam*, *dviśāṇyam*, *dviśāṇam*; *traiśāṇam*, *triśāṇyam*, *triśāṇam*.

*tena krītaṃ mūlyāt* (Pāṇini 4.1.47): After a word denoting price (*mūlya*) ending in the third case, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and others, as prescribed, occur in the sense of "purchased for that. Examples: *prāsthikaḥ*, *śatyaḥ*, *śatikaḥ*, *pañcakaḥ*. Why say "from a word denoting price"? [Counter-examples: *pāṇinā krītam* ("purchased with a hand"), *Devadattena krītam* ("purchased by Devadatta"). Because no specific number is understood in the commentary (*vṛtti*), here [the suffix does not apply] to *prasthābhyāṃ krītam* or *prasthaiḥ krītam*. However, when the specific meaning is understood, it certainly occurs: *dvikam*, *trikam*, *pañcakam*. *mudgaiḥ krītam* ("purchased with mung beans") → *maudgikam*.
*tasya vāpaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.48): [The suffixes occur] in the sense of "its sowing."

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and others occur, according to the rules, after a word ending in the sixth case in the sense of "sowing" (*vāpa*). That in which something is sown is called "sowing" (*vāpa*). [Example: *prāsthikaḥ*.
By the rule *pātrāt ṣṭhan* (Pāṇini 4.1.49), the suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs after a word ending in the sixth case in the sense of "sowing. [Examples: *pātrikaḥ*, *pātrikī*.

(4.1.50) *vāta-pitta-śleṣma-saṃnipātāt śamana-kopane*: The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words ending in the genitive case, such as *vāta* and others, in the sense of "pacifying" (*śamana*) or "provoking" (*kopana*). Examples: *vātikaḥ*, *paittikaḥ*, *ślaiṣmikaḥ*, *sāṃnipātikaḥ*.
(4.1.51) *nimitte saṃyoga-utpāte*: [The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs] in the sense of a cause (*nimitta*), whether it be a conjunction (*saṃyoga*) or a portent (*utpāta*).

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and others occur after words ending in the sixth case when the cause (*nimitta*) consists of a conjunction (*saṃyoga*) or a portent (*utpāta*). For example: "the cause of a hundred is a conjunction or a portent" results in *śatyaḥ* or *śatikaḥ*; likewise, *sāṃgrāmikaḥ*. Why specify "conjunction or portent"? [Consider: "Devadatta is the cause of a hundred. [In this case, the suffix is not applied. According to Pāṇini 4.1.52: "After a word of two syllables that is neither a number nor a measure, and excluding words beginning with *aśva*, the suffix *yat* is used."

After a word ending in the genitive case that consists of two syllables, excluding words meaning "number," "measure," "horse," and so forth, the suffix *yat* is added when the cause is a conjunction (*saṃyoga*) or a portent (*utpāta*). For example, "the conjunction or portent that is the cause of wealth" is *dhanya*. Why exclude "number" and so forth? [Because otherwise we would have] *pañcakaḥ*, *prāsthikaḥ*; *āśvikaḥ*, *āśmikaḥ*. How is *gavyam* formed? It is established by the rule *gor aci yat* (Pāṇini 5.1.2). [The words excluded are: *aśva*, *aśman*, *gaṇa*, *ūrṇā*, *umā*, *bhaṅga*, *varṣā*, *vasu*. [Also after] *brahmavarcasa* (by Pāṇini 4.1.53).
After the word *brahmavarcasa* ending in the sixth case, when there is a cause, a conjunction, or a portent, the suffix *yat* occurs. [The derivative is] *brahmavarcasyaḥ*.
From the word *putra* ending in the sixth case, when there is a cause, a conjunction, or a portent, the suffix *cha* occurs, as well as *yat*. [The derivatives are] *putrīyaḥ* and *putryaḥ*.

In the rule *pṛthivīsarvabhūmer añaṇau* (Pāṇini 4.1.55), the suffixes *añ* and *aṇ* are applied after these two words ending in the genitive case when they denote a cause, a connection, or a portentous event (*nimitta-saṃyoga-utpāta*). Thus: *pārthivaḥ* (lord of the earth) and *sārvabhaumaḥ* (lord of the whole world).
In the rule *īśvare* (Pāṇini 4.1.56): [the same suffixes are applied when denoting a ruler].
The suffixes *añ* and *aṇ* occur after the words *pṛthivī* and *sarvabhūmi*, ending in the sixth case, in the sense of "lord" (*īśvara*). Thus: *pārthivaḥ* and *sārvabhaumaḥ*.

Regarding the rule *tatra vidite* (Pāṇini 4.3.57): the suffixes *añ* and *aṇ* occur after the words *pṛthivī* and *sarvabhūmi* when they end in the seventh case, in the sense of "known therein. Thus: *pārthivaḥ* and *sārvabhaumaḥ*.
From the words *loka* and *sarvaloka*, when they end in the seventh case and denote "known," the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied. Thus: *laukikaḥ*, *sārvalaukikaḥ*.
[The suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied] in the sense of "that which is given here to this person as interest, profit, wages, or a toll" (Pāṇini 4.1.59).

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and others are applied according to the rules to a word ending in the nominative case (*prathamāntāt*) in the two senses of "given to this" (*asmin*) or "for this" (*asmai*), provided that the word ending in the nominative is one such as *vṛddhi* (interest/profit) and so forth. If five *vṛddhi*, or *āya*, or *lābha*, or *śulka*, or *utkoca* is given to this person or for this person, the form is *pañcakaḥ*. Similarly, *śatyaḥ* and *śatikaḥ*. Why is the mention of *vṛddhyādi* ("*vṛddhi* and so forth") made? [To exclude cases like: "five is given as the price (*mūlya*) in this.
[Next rule: *pūraṇārdhāṭ ṭhan* (Pāṇini 4.1.60).

The suffix *ṭhan* occurs after a word denoting a portion (*pūraṇa*) or after the word *ardha*, provided that the first-case form [of the stem] signifies "this is given to him" or "this is given in this," and provided that said first-case form begins with a *vṛddhi* vowel. For example: *pañcamo 'smai vāsmin vā vṛddhyādi dīyate* ("A fifth part is given to him, or in this [place], as an interest, etc. results in *pañcamikaḥ*; *ardhikaḥ*. Likewise, *pañcamikā* and *ardhikā*. Furthermore, the suffix *yac* occurs after the word *bhāga*. (Pāṇini 4.3.61)

After a word ending in the first case that denotes a "portion" (*bhāga*), the suffix *yat* and also *ṭhan* are applied in the two senses of "that which is given to this person" or "for this person," provided that the meaning is one of the [categories] beginning with *vṛddhi*. When a portion is given to this person or for this person: *bhāgyaḥ*, *bhāgikaḥ*. The word *bhāga* is a conventional term for half a *rūpaka*.
[The rule] *tad asya parimāṇam* (Pāṇini 5.1.57) [is also applicable].

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and others occur according to the prescribed rules after a word in the nominative case (*prathamāntāt*) in the sense of "belonging to this" (*asya*), provided that the nominative word denotes a measure (*parimāṇa*). For example: *prāsthiko vrīhiḥ* ("rice measured by a *prastha*"); *khāraśatikaḥ*, *khārasahasrikaḥ* ("worth a hundred or a thousand *khāras*"); *pañcakaḥ saṃghaḥ* ("a group of five"); *aṣṭakaṃ pāṇinīyaṃ sūtram* ("the eightfold collection of Pāṇini's aphorisms"); *pañcakaḥ pāṭho 'dhītaḥ* ("a lesson of five [verses] has been studied").

In the case of *pañcakāḥ śakunayaḥ* ("five-eroded birds"), the meaning of the base (*prakṛti*) is a collective (*samudāya*) that accepts an internal division of parts, such that "five" is their measure. The meaning of the word *ka* is the members of that collective as qualified by it. The repetition of the nominative case ending is for the purpose of re-enacting the rule; therefore, the elision (*luk*) prescribed by [Pāṇini 5.1.58] *saṃkhyādeḥ* does not occur. In *dviṣāṣṭikaḥ*, "two sixty-year periods" is his measure of life. [The following are the names of number-words: *paṅkti*, *viṃśati*, *triṃśat*, *catvāriṃśat*, *pañcāśat*, *ṣaṣṭi*.

*Saptatiḥ*, *aśītiḥ*, *navatiḥ*, and *śatam* are merely conventional designations (*saṃjñāśabda*), well-known in common usage, like *ayuta*, *prayuta*, *niyuta*, and so forth. According to Pāṇini 5.1.63, *pañcadaśad* is an irregularly formed term (*nipātana*) when the sense of a "group" (*varga*) is to be expressed. Thus, *pañcad* means a group of five (*pañcakaḥ*), and *daśad* means a group of ten (*daśakaḥ*).

*Stome ḍaṭ* (Pāṇini 4.1.64): After a word denoting a measure that ends in the nominative case, the suffix *ḍaṭ* occurs in the sense of "belonging to this," when a *stoma* (hymn-arrangement) is to be expressed. For example: *pañcadaśaḥ stomaḥ* ("a fifteen-fold hymn"), *pañcadaśī paṅktiḥ* ("a fifteen-fold row"). In the case of a *stoma*, the number itself constitutes the measure, and nothing else. *Triṃśaccatvāriṃśato brāhmaṇākhyāyāṃ ḍaṇ* (Pāṇini 4.1.65).

After these two [words] ending in the nominative case, in the sense of "belonging to this," the suffix *ḍaṇ* occurs when a *brāhmaṇa*—that is, one having that name—is to be expressed. Examples: *traiṃśāni brāhmaṇāni* ("Brāhmaṇas consisting of thirty [verses]"), *cātvāriṃśāni*. Why is the word "name" (*ākhyā*) mentioned? [To exclude cases like: *cātvāriṃśatkaḥ* ("consisting of forty"). Regarding the rule *bhṛti-vasnāṃśāḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.66):

after a word ending in the nominative case, in the sense of "belonging to this," the suffixes *ṭhañ* and others occur according to the prescribed rules, provided that the word ending in the nominative is "wages" (*bhṛti*), "price" (*vasna*), or "share" (*aṃśa*). Example: if five are the wages, price, or share belonging to him, it is *pañcakaḥ*.

*tat pacati droṇād aṇ ca* (4.1.67): After a word ending in the second case, when the sense of "he cooks that" is to be expressed, the suffix *aṇ* occurs after *droṇa*, as well as *ṭhañ*. [Examples: *drauṇī*, *drauṇikī*.
*saṃbhavaty avaharati ca* (4.1.68): [The same suffixes occur] when the senses of "it is possible" or "he brings forth" are to be expressed.

The suffixes *ṭhañ* and others are applied according to the rules after words ending in the second case, in the senses of "capable of containing," "harvesting," or "cooking. For example: that which is capable of containing, harvesting, or cooking one *prastha* is called *prāsthika*; likewise, *khārīka*. According to Pāṇini 4.1.69, the suffix *kha* optionally occurs after the words *pātra*, *ācita*, and *āḍhaka* when they end in the second case in the senses of "capable of containing" and so forth. Thus: from *pātra* we have *pātrīṇā* or *pātrikī*; from *ācita*, *ācitīnā* or *ācitikī*; and from *āḍhaka*, *āḍhakīnā* or *āḍhakikī*.
Pāṇini 4.1.70: *saṃkhyādeḥ ṣṭhaṃś ca* (and the suffix *ṣṭhan* after [words] beginning with a numeral).

After words beginning with a numeral and ending in *pātra*, etc., the suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs in the senses of "possible" (*sambhavati*), etc., and *khaś* optionally. Examples: *dvipātrikī*, *dvipātrīṇā*, *dvipātrī*; *dvyācitikī*, *dvyācitīnā*, *dvyācitā*; *dvyāḍhakikī*, *dvyāḍhakīnā*, *dvyāḍhakī*. Pāṇini 4.1.71: *kulijād vā* (after *kulija*, it is optional).

The suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs after the word *kulija* and others in the sense of "possible" (*saṃbhavati*) and so forth; or the suffix *kha* may be used, as well as whatever [suffixes] are otherwise prescribed. Since the rule "or *kha*" (*kho vā*) was already in force, the repetition of the word "or" (*vā*) here is for the purpose of allowing an option for the elision (*luk*) as well. Thus: *dvikulijikī*, *dvikulijīnā*, *dvaikulijikī*, *dvikulijī*.
[The rule] *vaṃśādibhyo harati vahaty āvahati bhārāt* (Pāṇini 4.4.72) [is also applicable].

The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after words such as *vaṃśa*, when they follow the word *bhāra* (burden) in the accusative case, in the sense of "carrying" (*harati*) and so forth. For example: one who carries, bears, or brings a load of bamboo is called *vāṃśabhārikaḥ*; likewise, *kauṭajabhārikaḥ*. Why does the rule specify "after *vaṃśa* and so forth"? [To exclude cases like: he carries a load (*bhāraṃ vahati*). Alternatively, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after words such as *vaṃśa* when they denote a "load" (*bhārabhūta*) and are in the accusative case, in the sense of "carrying" and so forth. For example: one who carries, bears, or brings bamboo that constitutes a load is called *vāṃśikaḥ*; likewise, *kauṭajikaḥ*.

What is the purpose of the word *bhārāt* [in the rule]? [Consider: *vaṃśaṃ harati* ("he carries a bamboo pole"). [The suffixes apply after] *vaṃśa*, *kuṭaja*, *balbaja*, *mūla*, *sthūṇā*, *akṣa*, *aśman*, *ikṣu*, and *khaṭvā*.
Regarding *dravya* and *vasna*: "After *dravya* and *vasna*, when [the sense of] 'carrying' and so forth is intended, *kan* occurs; after *vasna*, *ṭhan* occurs. Thus: *dravyakaḥ*, *vasnikaḥ*.

*Arhati* (Pāṇini 4.1.74): In the sense of "deserving," suffixes such as *ṭhañ* and others are applied according to the rules after a word ending in the accusative case. For example: *vastram arhati* ("he deserves a garment") results in *vāstrikaḥ*. Similarly, *śatyaḥ* and *śatikaḥ*. *Chedādibhyo nityam* (Pāṇini 4.1.75): After words beginning with *cheda*, the suffix is applied invariably [in the sense of "deserving"].

The suffix *ṭhañ* is invariably applied after words ending in the second case, such as *cheda*, in the sense of "one who deserves that. For example: one who always deserves cutting (*cheda*) is *chaiddhika*; one who deserves splitting (*bheda*) is *bhaiddhika*. [The bases include: *cheda*, *bheda*, *droha*, *doha*, *narta*, *karṣa*, *saṃprayoga*, *viprakarṣa*, *saṃpraśna*, *virāga*, and *viraṅga*. Regarding *śīrṣaccheda*: by rule 4.1.76, the suffix *yat* is applied after the word *śīrṣaccheda* ending in the second case in the sense of "one who invariably deserves that," and the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied. Thus: *śīrṣacchedyaḥ* and *śairṣacchedikaḥ*.

*yajñād ghaḥ* (4.1.77): After the word *yajña*, when it ends in the accusative case, the suffix *gha* occurs in the sense of "he is worthy of. Thus, *yajñiyaḥ*. One who is worthy of the sacrificial rite (*yajñakarma*) is also said to be "worthy of the sacrifice" (*yajñam asāv arhati*).
*pātrād yaś ca* (4.1.78).
The suffix *gha* occurs after the word *pātra* in the second case to express the sense of "deserving" (*arhati*), as well as the suffix *ya*. [Examples: *pātrīyaḥ*, *pātryaḥ*.

Regarding *daṇḍādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.79): the suffix *ya* occurs after words beginning with *daṇḍa* in the second case to express the sense of "deserving. [Examples: *daṇḍyaḥ*, *musalyaḥ*. The *daṇḍa*-group consists of: *daṇḍa*, *musala*, *madhuparka*, *kaśā*, *argha*, *medhā*, *megha*, *udaka*, *vadha*, *yuga*, and *ibha*.

(4.1.80) *dakṣiṇā-kaḍaṅgara-sthālī-bilāt chaś ca*: After the words *dakṣiṇā* and so forth, when ending in the accusative case, the suffix *cha* occurs in the sense of "deserving" (*arhati*), as well as the suffix *ya*. Deserving a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*): *dakṣiṇīyaḥ*, *dakṣiṇyaḥ*. Deserving chaff (*kaḍaṅgara*): *kaḍaṅgarīyaḥ*, *kaḍaṅgaryaḥ*. Deserving the contents of a cooking pot (*sthālībila*): *sthālībilīyaḥ*, *sthālībilyaḥ*. (4.1.81) *ārtvijīnaḥ*: [The suffix *khañ* occurs after the word *ṛtvij* in the sense of "belonging to the office of a priest"]. *ārtvijīnaḥ*.
This word is irregularly formed (*nipātita*) in the sense of "he deserves a priest" (*ṛtvijam arhati*) or "he deserves the work of a priest" (*ṛtvikkarma arhati*).

Regarding *śālīna* and *kaupīna* in the senses of "timid" (*adhṛṣṭa*) and "improper act" (*akārya*) respectively (Pāṇini 4.1.82): one who deserves to enter a hall (*śālām arhati praveṣṭum*) is called *śālīna* when he is timid; one who deserves to enter a well (*kūpam arhati praveṣṭum*) is called *kaupīna* when it refers to an improper act.

Regarding the rule *pārāyaṇaturāyaṇacāndrāyaṇaṃ vartayati* (Pāṇini 4.1.83): the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after these words ending in the accusative case when the sense is "he performs" (*vartayati*). Examples: *pārāyaṇikaḥ*, *tairāyaṇikaḥ*, *cāndrāyaṇikaḥ*. Regarding the rule *saṃśayam āpannaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.84): [the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *saṃśaya* in the accusative case when the sense is "fallen into doubt"]. Example: *sāṃśayikaḥ*.

The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after a word ending in the second case in the sense of "fallen into" (*āpanna*) when that word denotes a doubt; for example, *sāṃśayikaḥ*. [Pāṇini 4.1.85] The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after a word ending in the second case in the sense of "going" (*gacchati*) when that word denotes a *yojana*; for example, *yaujanikaḥ*.

(4.1.86) *krośayojanādeḥ śatād abhigamanārhe ca*: After words beginning with *krośa* and *yojana*, when the sense is "he goes a hundred [of them]" or "he is worthy of being approached from a hundred [of them]," the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs. For example: *krośaśataṃ gacchati* ("he goes a hundred *krośas*") becomes *krauśaśatikaḥ*; *yaujanaśatikaḥ*. Also, when he is worthy of being approached from a hundred *krośas*, it is *krauśaśatikaḥ*; *yaujanaśatikaḥ*. (4.1.87) *pathaḥ ṣṭhan*: After the word *pathin*, the suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs in these same senses.
The suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs after the word *pathin* ending in the second case in the sense of "one who goes. Thus: *pathikaḥ*, *pathikī*.

By the rule *ṇaḥ panthaś ca nityam* (Pāṇini 4.4.104), the suffix *ṇa* occurs after *pathin* ending in the second case in the sense of "one who always goes," and there is the substitution of *pantha* for *pathin*. One who always goes on the road: *pānthaḥ*, *pānthā*.

(4.1.89) *aja-śaṅku-uttara-vāri-jāṅgala-kāntāra-ādinā āhṛte ca*: The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after the word *pathin* preceded by *aja* and others, when it ends in the third case and signifies "one who goes" or "brought by means of. For example: one who goes by the goat-path (*ajapatha*) or is brought by the goat-path is *ājapathikaḥ*. Similarly: *śāṅkupathikaḥ*, *auttarapathikaḥ*, *vāripathikaḥ*, *jāṅgalapathikaḥ*, *kāntārapathikaḥ*.
(4.1.90) *sthalādinā*.

The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after the word *pathin* preceded by *sthala*, provided it ends in the third case, when the meanings "brought" (*āhṛta*) or "going" (*gacchati*) are intended. For example: *sthālapathikaḥ*. Regarding the rule 4.1.91, *madhukamarīcayor aṇ*: the suffix *aṇ* occurs after *sthālapatha* when the words *madhuka* or *marīca* are to be expressed. Thus: *sthālapathaṃ madhukaṃ* and *sthālapathaṃ marīcaṃ*.
"From time" (4.1.92):
this is a governing rule (*adhikāra*).
By means of it, [the sūtra] "completed by that" (4.1.93) [is governed].
The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words denoting time ending in the third case when the sense is "produced" (*nirvṛtta*). For example: *māsena nirvṛttam* → *māsikam*; *āhnikam*.

By the rule *tasmai bhṛto ’dhīṣṭaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.94), the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words denoting time ending in the fourth case in the two senses of "hired for" (*bhṛta*) or "appointed for" (*adhīṣṭa*). For example: *māsāya bhṛto ’dhīṣṭo vā* → *māsikaḥ*; *sāṃvatsarikaḥ*.

The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time ending in the second case, in the senses of "that which has occurred" (*bhūta*) or "that which is to occur" (*bhāvī*). For example: *māsaṃ bhūto bhāvī vā* = *māsikaḥ* ("lasting for a month" or "occurring within a month"); *sāṃvatsarikaḥ* ("lasting for a year"). Beyond this, the rule should be understood as applicable to the senses beginning with "completed" (*nirvṛtta*), as far as possible. [Pāṇini 4.3.19] states: *māsād vayasi yatkhañau* ("after *māsa*, the suffixes *yat* and *khañ* are applied in the sense of age").

When a period of time ending in the second case suffix is understood as a measure of age (*vayas*), the suffixes *khañ* and *kha* are applied to form words denoting that which has occurred (*bhūte*). For example: *māsaṃ bhūtaḥ* ("one who has existed for a month") becomes *māsyaḥ* or *māsīnaḥ*. In the compound *māsīnā duhitā asya* ("his daughter has been [born] for a month"), the feminine form *māsīnā* results in *māsīnāduhitṛkaḥ*; here, the substitution of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāvaḥ*) does not occur because of the rule *ādaij jheḥ* (Pāṇini 7.3.36). When the word *māsa-* is preceded by a numeral, the suffix *yap* is applied when age is implied; thus, from *dvau māsau bhūtaḥ*, we derive *dvimāsyaḥ*.

Pāṇini 4.1.98: *ṣaṣo ṇyac ca vā*. When a duration of six months (*ṣaṇmāsa*) is understood as a measure of age, the suffix *ṇyat* is applied, and *ya* is optionally applied as well. Examples: one who has existed for six months is *ṣāṇmāsyaḥ*, *ṣāṇmāsikaḥ*, or *ṣaṇmāsyaḥ*. Pāṇini 4.1.99: *ṭhaṃś cānyatra*. And the suffix *ṭhan* is applied in other cases [of duration].

After the word *vayas* ("age"), when it is other than "six" (*ṣaṣ*) and so on, the suffixes *ṭhan* and *ṇya* occur in the senses of "completed in," "hired for," "appointed for," "become in," or "destined to be in" a period of months. For example: completed in six months, hired for six months, or appointed for six months; having been born six months ago, or being due to be born in six months: *ṣaṇmāsikaḥ*, *ṣāṇmāsyaḥ*. By rule 4.1.100, *samāyāḥ khaḥ*: the suffix *kha* occurs after the word *samā* ("year") in the senses of "completed in" and so forth. For example: completed in a year, hired for a year, or appointed for a year; having been born a year ago, or being due to be born in a year: *samīnaḥ*.

Or, after a word beginning with a numeral (4.1.101), the suffix *kha* optionally occurs after a compound beginning with a numeral in the senses of "completed" (*nirvṛtta*) and so forth. For example: *dvisamīnaḥ*, *dvaisamikaḥ*.
[The suffix *thañ* also applies] after words meaning "night," "day," and "year" (4.1.102).

The suffix *kha* optionally occurs after words meaning "night" (*rātri*), "day" (*ahan*), and "year" (*saṃvatsara*), when they are preceded by a numeral, provided the sense is that of "completed" (*nirvṛtta*) and so forth. For example: *dvirātrīṇaḥ*, *dvairātrikaḥ*; *dvyahīnaḥ*, *dvaiyahnikaḥ*; *dvisaṃvatsarīṇaḥ*, *dvisāṃvatsarikaḥ*.
Regarding the rule *varṣāl luk ca* (Pāṇini 4.1.103):

after the word "year" (*varṣa*), when preceded by a numeral, the suffix *kha* optionally occurs in the senses of "completed" and so forth; furthermore, there is optionally the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *ṭhac*. For example: *dvivarṣīṇaḥ*, *dvivarṣaḥ*, *dvivārṣikaḥ*. However, in the sense of "destined to happen" (*bhāvin*), it is *dvaivarṣikaḥ*.

In the case of a living being (*prāṇin*), when a word beginning with a numeral denotes years (*varṣa*), there is *luṅ* (elision) of even the suffix *kha*, because of this subsequent rule. Thus: *dvivarṣaḥ* (two-year-old), *trivarṣaḥ* (three-year-old). The form *ṣaṣṭikāḥ* is established by the previous rule [Pāṇini 5.1.57] using the suffix *kan*: "those whose measure of ripening is sixty days" are *ṣaṣṭikāḥ* rice grains. Because it is a conventional term (*rūḍhi*), there is no over-extension (*atiprasaṅga*) to words such as *mudga* (beans) and the like.
By that [rule], [the forms] *sukara-kārya-labhya-parijayya* [are formed]. (Pāṇini 4.1.105)

The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time ending in the third case, in the senses of "easy to do," "work," "obtainable," or "conquerable. For example: that which is easy to do, a work, obtainable, or conquerable within a month is *māsika*. [This applies also] in the sense of "this is his period of student-life" (*tad asya brahmacarye*). (Pāṇini 4.1.106)

The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time ending in the second case (*dvitīyānta*), in the sense of the genitive (*ṣaṣṭhy-artha*), when "celibacy" (*brahmacarya*) is understood. For example: *māsaḥ asya brahmacaryam* ("a month is his celibacy") becomes *māsikaḥ brahmacārī* ("a month-long celibate"). Alternatively, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word ending in the first case (*prathamānta*) denoted by *tat*, in the sense of the genitive, when "celibacy" is to be expressed. For example: *māsaḥ asya brahmacaryasya* ("a month is of this celibacy") becomes *māsikam brahmacaryam* ("month-long celibacy"). [This applies] to the *mahānāmni* hymns and others, according to Pāṇini 4.1.107.

The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words such as *mahānāmni*, when they appear in the genitive case and denote a period of religious studentship (*brahmacarya*). For example: the studentship pertaining to the *mahānāmnī* verses is *māhānāmnikam*; likewise, *ādityavratikam* and *gaudānikam*. Regarding the rule *tac carati* (Pāṇini 4.1.108):

the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words such as *mahānāmni* when they appear in the accusative case in the sense of "one who performs that. Here, the word *tat* refers to the vow (*vrata*) of the *mahānāmnī* verses. One who performs that [vow] is called *māhānāmnikaḥ*.

(4.1.109) *Devavratādibhyo ḍiniḥ*: The suffix *ḍini* occurs after words such as *devavrata*, when they end in the accusative case, in the sense of "practicing" (*caratīti*). Examples: *devavratī*, *tilavratī*, *avāntaradīkṣī*. (4.1.110) *Aṣṭācatvāriṃśato ḍvuṃś ca*: [The suffix *ḍini*] and also the suffix *ḍvuṃ* occur after the word *aṣṭācatvāriṃśat*.

The suffixes *ḍvun* and *ḍini* occur after a word ending in the second case, in the sense of "he performs," provided that the object is the number forty-eight (*aṣṭācatvāriṃśat*). [Example: He performs the vow for forty-eight years: *aṣṭācatvāriṃśakaḥ*, *aṣṭācatvāriṃśī*. [Rule 4.1.111:

After the word *cāturmāsya* ending in the second case, in the sense of "he performs," the suffixes *ḍvun* and *ḍini* occur, and there is the elision of the letter *y*. [Example: He performs the *cāturmāsya* vow: *cāturmāsakaḥ*, *cāturmāsī*.

*tasya dakṣiṇā yajñebhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.3.112): the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words expressing sacrifices that end in the genitive case, in the sense of "sacrificial fee" (*dakṣiṇā*). For example: the sacrificial fee of the *agniṣṭoma* is *āgniṣṭomikī*; [the sacrificial fee] of the *vājapeya* is *vājapeyikī*. *tatra dīyate* (Pāṇini 4.3.113).

In this context, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after words denoting sacrifices ending in the locative case (*saptamyanta*) in the sense of "it is given there. For example: that which is given at the *agniṣṭoma* is called *āgniṣṭomikaḥ*; likewise, *vājapeyikaḥ* and *rājasūyikaḥ*. Regarding the rule *kālāt kāryaṃ ca bhavavat* (Pāṇini 4.3.114): after words denoting time ending in the locative case, the suffixes beginning with *ṭhañ*—just as they do in the sense of "occurring there" (*bhava*)—are applied in the two senses of "that which is to be done" (*kārya*) and "that which is given" (*dīyate*). For instance: that which is to be done or is given in a month is *māsikam*; similarly, *vāsantam*, *prāvṛṣeṇyam*, *vārṣikam*, *haimantam*, *haimanam*, and *sāyantanam*.

*Vyuṣṭādibhyo ’ṇ* (4.1.115): The suffix *aṇ* occurs after words beginning with *vyuṣṭa* when they appear in the locative case, in the two senses of "work is given" or "it is performed. For example, work is given at dawn (*vyuṣṭe*), hence *vaiyuṣṭam*. [Also] *nāityam*. The *vyuṣṭa*-group consists of: *vyuṣṭa*, *nitya*, *niṣkramaṇa*, *praveśana*, *tīrtha*, *saṃgrāma*, *saṃghāta*, *agnipada*, and *pīlumūla*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class). *Yathākathācāṇ ṇaḥ* (4.1.116): [The suffix] *aṇ* [is applied] after *yathākathāca*, and [the resulting form] takes the augment *ṇa*.

The suffix *ṇa* occurs after the word *yathākathāca* in the two senses of "the task is assigned" or "the fee is given. Thus, when the task is assigned according to whatever manner [one is told], it is *yāthākathācaṃ kāryam*; or when the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is given, it is *yāthākathācā dakṣiṇā*.

By the rule *tena hastād yat* (Pāṇini 4.4.117), the suffix *yat* occurs after the word *hasta* ending in the third case in these two senses: "the task is assigned by means of the hand" or "the fee is given by means of the hand"; thus, *hastena kāryaṃ dīyate* or *hastena dakṣiṇā dīyate* results in *hastyam*.

(4.1.118) The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after a word ending in the third case when the sense is "it looks beautiful by means of that. For example: *karṇaveṣṭakābhyāṃ śobhate* ("it looks beautiful with ear-ornaments") results in *kārṇaveṣṭakikaṃ mukham* ("a face beautiful with ear-ornaments"). Similarly, *vāstrayugikaṃ śarīram* ("a body beautiful with a pair of garments"). (4.1.119) The suffix *yat* occurs after the words *karman* and *veṣa*.

The suffix *yat* occurs after words ending in the third case—namely *karman* and *veṣa*—in the sense of "it shines" (*śobhate*). For example: *karmaṇyam śauryam* ("valor that shines through action") and *veṣyo naṭaḥ* ("an actor who shines in his costume").
[The suffix *yat*] also occurs after words such as *saṃtāpa* in the sense of "he prevails over" (*prabhavati*) them. (Pāṇini 4.1.120)

The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs in the sense of "capable of" (*prabhavati*) after words ending in the fourth case, such as *saṃtāpa* and others. For example: *saṃtāpāya prabhavati* = *sāṃtāpikaḥ* ("one who is capable of enduring heat"); *sāṃnāhikaḥ* ("one who is capable of donning armor"). [The suffix applies] after *saṃtāpa*, *saṃnāha*, *saṃgrāma*, *saṃyoga*, *saṃparāya*, *saṃveśa*, *nirghoṣa*, *nisarga*, *visarga*, *upasarga*, *pravāsa*, *upavāsa*, *saṃghāta*, *saṃpāda*, *sakta*, and *māṃsaudana*, even when these are used in their uncompounded forms. Furthermore, after *yoga*, the suffix *yac* also occurs. (Pāṇini 4.1.121)

In the sense of "it originates from" (*prabhavati*) [something] following a word ending in the fourth case (*caturthyanta*), the suffix *yat* occurs, as well as *ṭhañ*. For example: that which originates for the sake of yoga is *yogyaṃ* or *yaugikaṃ*.
By the rule *karmaṇa ukañ* (Pāṇini 4.1.122), the suffix *ukañ* occurs after a word ending in the fourth case in the sense of "it originates from" that action. For example: *kārmukam*.
*so 'sya prāptaḥ samayāt* (Pāṇini 4.1.123):

after the word *samaya*, when ending in the nominative case, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs in the sense of the genitive *asya*, provided that it is "attained" (*prāpta*). For example: "this has attained the [proper] time" (*samayaḥ prāpto 'sya*) = *sāmayika*.
*ṛtvādibhyo 'ṇ* (Pāṇini 4.1.124).

The suffix *aṇ* occurs after words beginning with *ṛtu*, when they appear in the nominative case, in the sense of the genitive "belonging to this," provided that those [seasons or times] have been reached (*prāpta*). For example: *ṛtuḥ prāpto 'sya* ("a season has arrived for him") results in *ārtavam*; likewise, *aupavastram* and *prāśitram*.

By the rule *kālād yat* (Pāṇini 4.3.11), the suffix *yat* occurs after the word *kāla* when it appears in the nominative case in the sense of the genitive "belonging to this," provided that [the time] has been reached. For example: *kālyaṃ himam* ("the cold has arrived at the proper time").

(4.1.126) After a word denoting time ending in the nominative case, the suffix *ṭhañ* occurs in the sense of the genitive (*asya*) provided that [the time] is "distant" (*prakṛṣṭa*). If the time is distant for him, it is a *kālika* debt.
(4.1.127) [The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs] in the sense of "purpose" (*prayojana*).

The suffix *ṭhañ* occurs after a word ending in the nominative case in the sense of the genitive (*asya*), provided that the thing denoted is the purpose (*prayojana*). For example, "Indramaha is his purpose" results in *aindramahikaḥ*.
According to Pāṇini 4.1.128, *ekāgārāc caure*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied specifically to the word *caura* (thief) when the meaning is "that is his purpose," derived from the word *ekāgāra*.

Thus, "a thief whose purpose is a single house" is *aikāgārikaś cauraḥ*. Why specify "thief"? [Consider: "a mendicant whose purpose is a single house" (*ekāgāraṃ prayojanam asya bhikṣoḥ*). In this case, the suffix is not applied because the referent is not a thief.

*Ākālāṭ ṭhaṃś ca* (Pāṇini 4.1.129): From the word *ākāla*, in the sense of "that is its purpose," the suffixes *ṭhan* and *ṭhañ* occur. That which is its very time of origin lasts for that long: *ākālikaḥ anadhyāyaḥ* (a suspension of Vedic study lasting as long as [the cause]); *ākālikā vidyut* (lightning lasting as long as [the cause]). [The feminine form is] *ākālikī*. *Cūḍādibhyo ’ṇ* (Pāṇini 4.1.130).

The suffix *aṇ* occurs after the words *cūḍā* and others in the sense of "that for which this is the purpose. For example, that for which the *cūḍā* (topknot ceremony) is the purpose is *cauḍam*—namely, a *śrāddha* rite. Regarding the rule *viśākhāṣāḍhān manthadaṇḍayoḥ* (Pāṇini 4.2.131): the suffix *aṇ* occurs after the words *viśākhā* and *āṣāḍhā* in the sense of "that for which this is the purpose," provided that *mantha* (churning stick) and *daṇḍa* (staff) are the meanings to be expressed. Thus, a churning stick for which the *viśākhā* constellation is the purpose is *vaiśākhaḥ*; a staff for which the *āṣāḍhā* constellation is the purpose is *āṣāḍhaḥ*. Why specify "of the churning stick and the staff"? [To exclude other meanings: *vaiśākhikaḥ* and *āṣāḍhikaḥ* (referring to certain festivals or periods).

(4.1.132) *utthāpanādibhyaś chaḥ*: After the words beginning with *utthāpana*, the suffix *cha* occurs in the sense of "that is its purpose. Thus, we have *utthāpanīyam* and *upasthāpanīyam*. [The list of bases is: *utthāpana*, *upasthāpana*, *anupravacana*, *praveśana*, *saṃveśana*, *anuveśana*, *anuvacana*, *anuvāsana*, *anurohaṇa*, *ārohaṇa*, *ārambhaṇa*, and those derived from the roots *viśi*, *pūri*, *pad*, *ruhi*, *samāpi*, provided they are preceded by another word and do not end in the suffix *ān*.

*gṛhapraveśanīyam* (suitable for entering a house), *prapāpūraṇīyam* (suitable for filling a water-distribution shed), *aśvaprapadanīyam* (suitable for horses to enter), *prāsādārohaṇīyam* (suitable for ascending a palace), and *vyākaraṇasamāpanīyam* (suitable for completing the study of grammar).

According to *svargādibhyo yat* (Pāṇini 4.1.133), the suffix *yat* occurs after words such as *svarga* and others in the sense of "that which has this as its purpose. Thus: *svargyam* (leading to heaven), *dhanyam* (bringing wealth), *yaśasyam* (bringing fame), *āyuṣyam* (conducive to long life), and *kāmyam* (desirable).

*Puṇyāhavācanādibhyo luk* (4.1.134): After the words *puṇyāhavācana* and others, there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *ṭhañ* in the sense of "that is its purpose. Examples: *puṇyāhavācanam*, *svastivācanam*, *śāntivācanam*. *Ive vatiḥ* (4.1.135).

The suffix *vat* occurs in the sense of *iva* ("like" or "as"). He behaves like a king: *rājavat*. He has conducted himself like a king: *rājavat*. His conduct is like that of a Brahmin: *brāhmaṇavat*. There are palaces in Pāṭaliputra as in Mathurā: *mathurāvat*. I see you as I would see a god: *devavat*. He descends from his seat as if from a mountain: *parvatavat*. He gives to Devadatta as if to a Brahmin: *brāhmaṇavat*. In this case as well, the desired meaning is indeed obtained by the rule *tadarham* (Pāṇini 5.1.117).

"Whatever is worthy of seeing is [the object] of the god (*devam arhati yad darśanam*); whatever is worthy of descending is [the object] of the mountain (*parvatam arhati yad avarohaṇam*); whatever is worthy of giving is [the object] of the Brahmin (*brāhmaṇam arhati yad dānam*). If this is so, then since the sense of "like" (*iva*) exists, it is established by this very rule even when there is equality of qualities (*guṇasāmya*): "as fat as Devadatta" (*Devadatta iva sthūlaḥ*), or "as fat as Devadatta" (*Devadattavat sthūlaḥ*). Also from equality of qualities: "like a blind man" (*andhavat*), "like a dull man" (*jaḍavat*). Even in the case of equality of substance (*dravyasāmya*): "possessing cows like Devadatta" (*Devadattavad gomān*). Since similarity of action (*kriyāsāmya*) is also possible here, it should occur everywhere.
Regarding that [suffix], the suffixes *tva* and *tal* are used to express the state [of being so] (*tasya bhāvas tvatalau*, Pāṇini 5.1.119).

The suffixes *tva* and *tal* occur after a word ending in the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*) to express the state (*bhāva*). What, then, is "state"? It is that from which both the designation and the cognition arise; it is the ground for the application (*pravṛttinimitta*) of a word. The state of a white cloth is "whiteness" (*śuklatva*) or "the state of being white" (*śuklatā*); here, the quality (*guṇa*) is the state. The state of the quality "white" is "whiteness" or "the state of being white"; here, the universal (*jāti*) of the white quality is the state. "Cowness" (*gotva*) or "the state of being a cow" (*gotā*) is the universal of the cow. "Cook-ness" (*pācakatva*), "staff-bearer-ness" (*daṇḍitva*), "horned-ness" (*viṣāṇitva*), and "king's-man-ness" (*rājapuruṣatva*) refer to the state of being related to an action and so forth.

The states of being Devadatta, the moon, or the sun are universals (*sāmānya*) consisting of specific conditions (*avasthā-viśeṣa*). The state of being space or the state of being non-existence are universals consisting of metaphorical distinctions (*upacarita-bheda-sāmānya*).
Regarding the rule *naño 'nanyārthe* (Pāṇini 5.1.137):

after the negative particle *nañ*, when it functions in the sense of "not other than" (*ananyapadārtha*), the suffixes *tva* and *tal* alone occur to denote the abstract state (*bhāva*). Examples: *amṛdutvam*, *amṛdutā*. Why is *nañaḥ* ("after the negative particle") stated? [Consider: *mārdavam* (softness). Why is *ananyārthe* ("in the sense of not other than") stated? [Consider: "He does not possess skill," i.e., *apaṭuḥ*; the state of being *apaṭu* is *āpaṭavam*.

After the words *catuḥ* and so forth, when preceded by the negative particle *nañ*, the suffixes *tva* and *tal* optionally occur in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*). *Acaturatvam*, *acaturatā*, *ācaturyam*. *Asaṃgatatvam*, *asaṃgatatā*, *āsaṃgatyam*. *Alavaṇatvam*, *alavaṇatā*, *ālavaṇyam*. *Avaḍatvam*, *avaḍatā*, *āvaḍyam*. *Abudhatvam*, *abudhatā*, *ābudhyam*. *Akatatvam*, *akatatā*, *ākatyam*. *Arasatvam*, *arasatā*, *ārasyam*. *Alasatvam*, *alasatā*, *ālasyam*.
The suffix *iman* occurs after the group of words beginning with *pṛthu*. (Pāṇini 5.1.122)

The suffix *imanij* occurs after the words beginning with *pṛthu* to denote the abstract state (*bhāva*). [Examples: *prathimā*, *pārthavam*, *pṛthutvam*, *pṛthutā*; *mradimā*, *mārdavam*, *mṛdutvam*, *mṛdutā*. The words are: *pṛthu*, *mṛdu*, *mahat*, *paṭu*, *aṇu*, *laghu*, *bahu*, *sādhu*, *āśu*, *uru*, *guru*, *bahula*, *khaṇḍa*, *caṇḍa*, *akiñcana*, *bāla*, *hoḍa*, *pāka*, *vatsa*, *manda*, *svādu*, *ṛju*, *hrasva*, *dīrgha*, *kṣudra*, *kṣipra*, *priya*.
Furthermore, the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied after words denoting color (*varṇa*) and after *dṛḍha* and others. (Pāṇini 5.1.123–124)

The suffix *ṣyañ* occurs in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) after words expressing specific qualities (*varṇaviśeṣa*) and after *dṛḍha* and others; alternatively, the suffix *imanij* may be used. For example: *śauklyam*, *śuklimā*, *śuklatvam*, *śuklatā*; *dārḍhyam*, *draḍhimā*, *dṛḍhatvam*, *dṛḍhatā*. The letter *ṣ* [in *ṣyañ*] is for the purpose of [triggering] the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*: *aucitī*, *yāthākāmī*. The list includes: *dṛḍha*, *parivṛḍha*, *vṛṣa*, *bhṛśa*, *kṛśa*, *cukra*, *āmra*, *āmla*, *tṛṣṇā*, *lavaṇa*, *śīta*, *uṣṇa*, *jaḍa*, *badhira*, *mūka*, *mūrkha*, *paṇḍita*, *madhura*.

[Furthermore, the suffix *ṣyañ* occurs] in the sense of action (*karman*) as well as state (*bhāva*) after words denoting qualities (*guṇavacana*) and after the *brāhmaṇa*-class [of words]. (Pāṇini 5.1.123–124).

The suffix *ṣyañ* optionally occurs after words expressing a quality (*guṇa*) and after words such as *brāhmaṇa*, in the sense of an action (*karman*) or a state (*bhāva*). For example, the action or state of being dull (*jaḍa*) is: *jāḍyam*, *jaḍimā*, *jaḍatvam*, *jaḍatā*. [Similarly: *brāhmaṇyam*, *brāhmaṇatvam*, *brāhmaṇatā*; *māṇavyam*, *māṇavatvam*, *māṇavatā*. After the words *brāhmaṇa*, *māṇava*, *vāḍava*, and *arhat*, the augment *num* is also inserted.

Arhatship—thief, rogue, messenger, propitiate, offend, single-natured, double-natured, triple-natured, other-natured, knower of the field, conversant, cohabiting, conversing, talkative, head-smiter, standing together, standing unevenly, standing supreme, standing in the middle, non-lord, skillful, fickle, clever, wise, familyless, slanderous, childish, lazy, wicked man, king, merchant, domestic priest.

The suffix *yañ* is applied after the following words when their own sense (*svārtha*) is intended: *khaṇḍika*, *paryantadeśa*, *rājapuruṣa*, *gaṇapati*, *adhipati*, *gaḍula*, *dāyāda*, *viśasti*, *viyāta*, and *cāturvarṇya*, etc. Examples: *cāturvarṇyam* (the four castes), *cāturvedyam* (the four Vedas), *cāturāśramyam* (the four stages of life), *trailokyam* (the three worlds). After the word *sarvaveda*, when both members [of the compound] end in *ai* or *au*, the suffix *yañ* is applied: *sārvavaidyam*. This is an *ākṛtigaṇa* (an open class of words). Furthermore, the suffix *ya* is applied after *sakhi*, *dūta*, and *vaṇij*: (Pāṇini 4.1.142).

After the words *sakhi* and others, the suffix *yañ* optionally occurs in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) and action (*karman*). Thus: *sakhyaṃ*, *sakhitvaṃ*, *sakhitā*; *dūtyaṃ*, *dūtatvaṃ*, *dūtatā*, *daityaṃ*; *vaṇijyā*, *vaṇiktvaṃ*, *vaṇiktā*, *vāṇijyaṃ*.

Regarding *steyaṃ* (Pāṇini 4.4.143): in the sense of the state or action of a thief (*stena*), the form *steya* is irregularly derived (*nipātita*) with the suffix *yañ* optionally. Thus: *steyaṃ*, *stainyaṃ*, *stenatvaṃ*, *stenatā*.

*Kapi-jñātyor ḍhak* (4.1.144): After these two, the suffix *ḍhak* optionally occurs in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) or action (*karman*). Thus: *kāpeyam*, *kapitvam*, *kapitā*; *jñāteyam*, *jñātitvam*, *jñātitā*. [In cases such as] *vānaspatyam* and *paurohityam*, the form is established by the suffix *ṣyañ* itself due to their inclusion in the *brāhmaṇa*-class. *Prāṇi-jāti-vayo-'rthodgātrādibhyo 'ñ* (4.1.145): After words denoting species of living beings, age, and the group beginning with *udgātṛ*, the suffix *añ* is applied.

The suffix *añ* optionally occurs after words denoting species of living beings, after words expressing age, and after [the class of] *udgātṛ* and so forth, in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) or an action (*karman*). Examples: *āśvam*, *aśvatvam*, *aśvatā* (from *aśva*); *kaumāram*, *kumāratvam*, *kumāratā* (from *kumāra*); *audgātram*, *udgātṛtvam*, *udgātṛtā*; *aunnetram*, *unnetṛtvam*, *unnetṛtā*. [The following belong to the *udgātṛ* group: *udgātṛ*, *unnetṛ*, *pratihartṛ*, *praśāstṛ*, *hotṛ*, *kartṛ*, *bhartṛ*, *rathagaṇaka*, *pattigaṇaka*, *suṣṭhu*, *duṣṭhu*, *adhvaryu*, *vadhū*, *subhaga*.
Pāṇini 4.1.146 states: "The suffix *aṇ* occurs after words ending in *hāyana* and after the *yuvan* group."

The suffix *aṇ* optionally occurs after words ending in *hāyana* and after the group beginning with *yuvan*, in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) or action (*karman*). Examples: *dvaihāyanam*, *dvihāyanatvam*, *dvihāyanatā*; *yauvanam*, *yuvatvam*, *yuvatā*; *sthāviram*, *sthaviratvam*, *sthaviratā*.

[The suffix *cha* is applied] after *yuvan*, *sthavira*, *hotṛ*, *yajamāna*, and *puruṣa* when not in a compound; after *bhrātṛ*, *kutuka*, *kanduka*, *śravaṇa*, *kamaṇḍalu*, *kustrī*, *sustrī*, *duḥstrī*, *suhṛdaya*, *suhṛd*, *durhṛd*, *subhrātṛ*, *durbhrātṛ*, *vṛṣala*, *parivrājaka*, *brahmacārin*, and *anṛśaṃsa-hṛdaya* when not in a compound; and after *capala*, *kuśala*, *nipuṇa*, *piśuna*, *kutūhala*, and *kṣetrajña*, as well as *śrotriya*, with the elision of the *ya* [of *śrotriya*], resulting in *śrautra*; and because of its inclusion in the *manojñādi* group, it also forms *śrautriyaka*.
[The suffix *ka* is applied] to a light *ik* vowel that does not belong to *kavi*. (Pāṇini 4.1.147)

After a light vowel, the suffix *ika* occurs; after a word ending in such an *ika*, the suffix *aṇ* optionally occurs in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) or object (*karman*), provided the word does not mean "poetry" (*kavi*). Examples: *śaucam*, *śucitvam*, *śucitā*; *pārthavam*, *pṛthutvam*, *pṛthutā*. Why "after a light vowel"? Consider *pāṇḍutvam*. Why "ending in *ika*"? Consider *rasatvam*. Why "not meaning poetry"? Consider *kāvyam*, which takes the suffix *ṣyañ* because it belongs to the *brāhmaṇa*-class. [Next rule:

After a word whose penultimate letter is *y*, whose penultimate syllable is heavy (*gurūpottama*), and which is not well-known as having a nominal suffix (*asuprakhyāt*), the suffix *vuñ* occurs. (Pāṇini 4.1.148)

The suffix *vuñ* optionally occurs after a word ending in *ya*, having a heavy syllable (*guru*) in the penultimate position (*upottama*), provided it is not a well-known name (*suprakhyavarjita*), when expressing the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) or an object (*karman*). Examples: *rāmaṇīyakam*, *ramaṇīyatvam*, *ramaṇīyatā*; *sāhāyakam*, *sahāyatvam*, *sahāyatā*, *sāhāyyam*. Why "ending in *ya*"? Consider *vitānatvam*. Why "having a heavy syllable in the penultimate position"? Consider *kṣatriyatvam*. Why "not being a well-known name"? Consider *suprakhyatvam* and *sauprakhyam*. [Furthermore, the suffix *aṇ* occurs] after compounds meaning "and so forth" (*cārtha*), after *samāsa*, and after words beginning with *manojña* (Pāṇini 4.1.149).

After a compound whose final member is *artha*, as well as after words such as *manojña* and others, the suffix *vuñ* optionally occurs in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) or action (*karman*). Examples: *śaiṣyopādhyāyikā* (the state of teacher and pupil), *śiṣyopādhyāyatvam*, *śiṣyopādhyāyatā*; *mānojñakam* (loveliness), *manojñatvam*, *manojñatā*; *praiyarūpakam* (beauty), *priyarūpatvam*, *priyarūpatā*.

*manojña*, *priyarūpa*, *abhirūpa*, *ahorūpa*, *kalyāṇa*, *medhāvin*, *āḍhya*, *kulaputra*, *chāndasa*, *chāttra*, *śrotriya*, *cora*, *dhūrta*, *viśvadeva*, *yuvan*, *grāmaputra*, *grāmaṣaṇḍa*, *grāmakumāra*, *amuṣyaputra*, *amuṣyakula*, *śarapattra*. [The suffix *cha* is applied after words denoting lineage (*gotra*) and Vedic school (*caraṇa*), when praise or censure is understood. (Pāṇini 4.1.150)

The suffix *vuñ* optionally occurs after words denoting a lineage (*gotra*) or a school of Vedic recitation (*caraṇa*), when expressing an abstract state (*bhāva*) or an action (*karman*), provided they relate to the context of praising (*ślāghā*) and so forth. Examples: *Gārgikayā ślāghate* (He praises by means of being a descendant of Garga), or *Gārgyatvena ślāghate*. *Kāṭhikayā ślāghate*, or *Kaṭhatvena ślāghate*. *Gārgikayātyākurute* (He treats with contempt by means of being a descendant of Garga), or *Gārgyatvenātyākurute*. *Kāṭhikayātyākurute*, or *Kaṭhatvenātyākurute*. *Gārgikām avagatavān* (or *prāptavān*) (He has understood or attained the state of being a descendant of Garga). *Kāṭhikām avagatavān* (or *prāptavān*) (He has understood or attained the state of being a follower of the Kaṭha school). Why "in the context of praising and so forth"? *Gārgyatvam*, *Kaṭhatvam* (The state of being a descendant of Garga; the state of being a follower of the Kaṭha school). [From here on, the rule for the suffix *cha* applies: *ṛtvigbhyaś chaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.151).

The suffix *cha* optionally occurs after words denoting specific officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) in the senses of abstract state (*bhāva*) or action (*karman*). For example: *acchāvākīyam* or *acchāvākatvam*; *mitrāvaruṇīyam* or *mitrāvaruṇatvam*.

Regarding the word *brahman*, [Pāṇini 4.1.152] states that only the suffix *tva* occurs after *brahman* when it denotes an officiating priest; thus, *brahmatvam*. However, when *brahman* is used as a synonym for a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*), both *brahmatvam* and *brahmatā* are possible.

The first quarter of the fourth chapter is completed. (4.2.1) *dhānyebhyaḥ kṣetre khañ*: After words denoting grains (*dhānya*) ending in the genitive case, the suffix *khañ* is applied when the sense is "field" (*kṣetra*). Example: *kulatthānāṃ kṣetram* ("the field of *kulattha* beans") becomes *kaulatthīnam*. Why "after words denoting grains"? Witness: *tṛṇānāṃ kṣetram* ("a field of grass"). Why "when the sense is 'field'"? Witness: *mudgānāṃ kusūlaḥ* ("a granary of mung beans").

*Vrīhi-śāler ḍhak* (4.2.2): The suffix *ḍhak* occurs after the words *vrīhi* and *śāli* when they are in the genitive case, provided that the field (*kṣetra*) is the sense intended. Thus: *vraiheyam*, *śāleyam*. *Yavayavaka-ṣaṣṭikād yat* (4.2.3): The suffix *yat* occurs after the words *yava*, *yavaka*, and *ṣaṣṭika* [when denoting the field].
From words such as *yava* ending in the genitive case, [the suffix] *yat* is applied when referring to what grows in a field: *yavyam*, *yavakyam*, *ṣaṣṭikyam*.
Regarding the rule "optionally after *tila*, *māṣa*, *umā*, *bhaṅgā*, and *aṇu*" (Pāṇini 4.2.4):

after *tila* and the others, *yat* is optionally applied when referring to a field. Thus: *tilyam* or *tailīnam*; *māṣyam* or *māṣīṇam*; *umyam* or *aumīnam*; *bhaṅgyam* or *bhāṅgīnam*; *aṇavyam* or *āṇavīnam*.
(4.2.5) *khañ* [is added] after *aśva* when that which is to be traversed in one day is meant.

After the word *aśva* ending in the genitive case, the suffix *khañ* occurs when the distance to be traveled in one day is indicated. Example: *āśvīna adhvā* ("a path to be covered in one day by horse").
(4.2.6) [The suffix *khañ* is added] after *goṣṭha* when the sense of "past" (*bhūta*) is expressed.

*Goṣṭha* means "that in which cows stand"; from this word *goṣṭha*, when it denotes something that has existed (*bhūta*) in the past, the suffix *khañ* occurs in its own sense (*svārthe*). Example: *gauṣṭhīnaḥ*. Why does it say "having existed" (*bhūta*)? [Because] *goṣṭhaḥ vartate* ("a cowpen exists"). *Sāptapadīnaṃ sakhye* (Pāṇini 4.3.70):

The form *sāptapadīna* is prescribed by way of a technical substitution (*nipātana*) when friendship (*sakhyam*) is implied. It is acquired through seven steps (*saptabhiḥ padair avāpyate*), hence it is called *sāptapadīna* friendship. A *sāptapadīna* friend; a *sāptapadīna* companion.
(4.2.8) *sarvacarmaṇā kṛtaḥ*:

after the word *sarvacarman* ending in the third case, the suffix *khañ* occurs in the sense of "made. Example: *sārvacarmīṇaḥ*. Others, however, maintain that this is an *asamartha-samāsa* (an irregular compound): "made entirely from leather," hence *sārvacarmīṇaḥ*. (4.2.9) *khaḥ*: [The suffix] *kha* [is applied].

The suffix *kha* occurs after a word ending in the third case (*tṛtīyā*) denoting "all" (*sarva*) when the sense of "made of" (*kṛta*) is expressed. Example: *sarvacarmīṇaḥ* ("made entirely of leather"). Regarding the rule *yathāmukhasammukhaṃ dṛśyate 'smin* (Pāṇini 4.2.10): the suffix *kha* occurs after the words *yathāmukha* and *sammukha*, both in the nominative case, in the sense of "that in which something is seen. Example: *yathāmukhaṃ dṛśyate 'smin* ("that in which one's face is seen") = *yathāmukhīnaḥ*, such as a mirror; likewise, *sammukhīnaḥ*. In the term *yathāmukham*, the compound is formed by irregular derivation (*nipātana*) even in the sense of similarity. Thus, *samam mukham* (an equal face) is *sammukham*, or *samyak mukham* (a properly directed face) is also *sammukham*.

[The suffix] *kha* occurs after [words] beginning with *sarva*, ending in the second case, such as *pathin* and others, when the sense is "it pervades" (*vyāpnoti*). (Pāṇini 4.2.11) Examples: *sarvapathaṃ vyāpnoti* → *sarvapathīnaḥ*; *sarvāṅgīṇaḥ*; *sarvakarmīṇaḥ*; *sarvapattrīṇaḥ*; *sarvapātrīṇaḥ*.
[The suffix] *kha* occurs after the word *āprapada* when the sense is "it reaches up to" (*prāpnoti*). (Pāṇini 4.2.12)

*Padāgram* means the tip of the foot; *āprapadam* means as far as the tip of the feet. After a word ending in the second case, the suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "reaching unto. For example: *āprapadīnaḥ paṭaḥ* ("a cloth reaching down to the tips of the feet"). Regarding *anupadaṃ baddhā* (Pāṇini 4.2.13):
after the word *anupada* ending in the second case, the suffix *kha* occurs when the meaning is "bound. For example: *anupadīnā upānat* ("a shoe that fits exactly the size of the foot").

*Ayānayaṃ neyaḥ* (4.2.14): *Ayaḥ* means clockwise; *anayaḥ* means counter-clockwise. Both together constitute *ayānaya*. From that [compound], when the sense is "to be led" (*neye*), the suffix *kha* occurs after a word ending in the second case. Example: *ayānayīnaḥ śāraḥ* ("a die that can be led both ways"). *Sarvānnam atti* (4.2.15).

The suffix *kha* occurs after a word ending in the accusative case meaning "all food" (*sarvānna*) in the sense of "he eats. For example: *sarvānnaṃ bhakṣayati* ("he eats all food") becomes *sarvānnīnaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ* ("a Brahmin who eats all food").

The suffix *kha* occurs after words ending in the accusative case such as *parāvara*, *parapara*, and *putrapautra* in the sense of "he experiences. *Para* and *avara* together form *parāvara*; the change to *u* (*utvam*) occurs by way of a formal rule (*nipātana*). *Para* and *paratara* together form *paraṃpara*; the addition of the nasal augment (*num*) occurs by way of a formal rule. Thus we have: *parāvarīṇaḥ*, *paraṃparīṇaḥ*, and *putrapautrīṇaḥ*.

(4.2.17) *pārāvāra-*, *avārapāra-*, *atyanta-*, and *anukāma-* [take the suffix *kha*] when combined with the word *gāmī*. After the words *pārāvāra-* and the others ending in the second case, whether used in combination or individually, the suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "one who goes to" (*gāmī*). Examples: *pārāvāraṃ gāmī* → *pārāvārīṇaḥ*; *avārapārīṇaḥ*; *avārīṇaḥ*; *pārīṇaḥ*; *atyantīnaḥ*; *anukāmīnaḥ*.
(4.2.18) *anu-gvam* [is formed with the suffix *kha*] in the sense of "sufficiently" (*alam*).
After the word *anu-gu*, ending in the second case, the suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "one who goes sufficiently" (*alaṃ-gāmī*). Example: *anugavīnaḥ*.
Regarding the rule *adhvānaṃ yañ ca* (Pāṇini 4.2.19):
after the word *adhvan*, ending in the second case, the suffix *yañ* occurs, and also *kha*, in the sense of "one who goes sufficiently. Examples: *adhvanīnaḥ*, *adhvanyaḥ*.

*abhyamitraṃ chaś ca* (Pāṇini 4.2.20): After the word *abhyamitra* ending in the accusative case, the suffix *kha* occurs in the sense of "one who goes sufficiently [to meet]," and also the suffixes *cha* and *yac*. [Examples: *abhyamitrīṇaḥ*, *abhyamitrīyaḥ*, *abhyamitryaḥ*.
*samāṃsamīnādyaśvīnāgavīnāḥ* (Pāṇini 4.2.21).

These words ending in *kh* are treated as irregular forms (*nipātana*). A cow that calves every year is called *samāṃsamīnā*. One that calves today or tomorrow is *adyaśvīnā*. A laborer who works until the payment of a cow or its delivery is *āgavīnaḥ*. [The suffix *kha* is applied] after the words *aṣaḍakṣa*, *āśitaṅgu*, *alaṃkarman*, *alaṃpuruṣa*, and those ending in *adhi* (Pāṇini 4.1.22).

*Aṣaḍakṣaḥ*: because there are not six eyes in this, it is *aṣaḍakṣa*. *Āśitaṅguḥ*: cows have been fed in this [place]; the augment *num* occurs here due to irregular derivation (*nipātana*). *Alaṃ karmaṇe*, *alaṃ puruṣāya*: a compound according to Pāṇini 2.2.24 (*kuprādayaḥ*). *Rājany adhi*: by this very irregular derivation (*nipātana*), a compound occurs in the domain of the suffix *kha*. From these, the suffix *kha* occurs in its own sense (*svārthe*). Examples: *aṣaḍakṣīṇo mantraḥ* (a counsel not accessible to six eyes), *āśitaṃgavīnam araṇyam* (a forest where cattle have been fed). *Alaṃkarmīṇaḥ*, *alaṃpuruṣīṇaḥ*, *rājādhīnaḥ*. According to Pāṇini 4.2.23: "After *adhi*, *añc* optionally [takes *kha*]."

The suffix *kha* optionally occurs in the sense of the base itself after the root *añc*, when it ends in *kvip*, provided that a direction (*diś*) is not being expressed. For example: *prāk* and *prācīnam*; *apāk* and *apācīnam*; *udak* and *udīcīnam*. Why does the rule specify "not a direction"? [To exclude cases such as: *prācī dik* ("the eastern direction"). Regarding the rule *pīlvādīnāṃ pāke kuṇap* (Pāṇini 4.3.167): the suffix *kuṇap* occurs after words beginning with *pīlu* when they are in the genitive case and denote "ripening. Examples: *pīlukuṇaḥ* ("the ripening of the *pīlu* fruit"). The *pīlvādi* group consists of: *pīlu*, *karkandhū*, *śamī*, *karīra*, *kuvala*, *badara*, *aśvattha*, *khadira*, and *puṣpa*.

*Jāhac* is added after *karṇa* and others in the sense of "at the root" (4.2.25). After words beginning with *karṇa* ending in the genitive case, the suffix *jāhac* occurs in the sense of "at the root. Examples: *karṇajāham*, *akṣijāham*. [The list of bases is: *karṇa*, *akṣi*, *nakha*, *mukha*, *keśa*, *pāda*, *gulpha*, *bhrū*, *śṛṅga*, *danta*, *oṣṭha*, *puṣpa*.
